articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Day 4: Mirabai Chanu ends Asiad medal wait; India win two skeet bronzes in shooting
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Mirabai Chanu finally ended her long wait for an Asian Games medal, winning silver in the women's 49kg category on Wednesday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Mirabai Chanu finally ended her long wait for an Asian Games medal, winning silver in the women's 49kg category on Wednesday.The 32-year-old lifted a total of 198kg (88kg+111kg) to finish second. The medal was India's first Asian Games weightlifting medal since Karnam Malleswari won silver in 1998.Mirabai had been chasing an Asian Games medal since 2014. The Tokyo Olympic silver medallist once again showed her class on the big stage and added another major medal to her career.With a familiar grin on her face, she made light work of the heavy lifts before declaring that her "life is now complete."Skeet shooters save the day for IndiaIt was a mixed day for India at the shooting range.The much-anticipated women's 10m air pistol team of double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker, Suruchi Singh and Esha Singh could not win a medal in either the team or individual events.Bhaker was the only Indian from the trio to qualify for the individual final, but she finished fifth.The 24-year-old Paris Olympics bronze medallist later broke down while speaking about the emotional impact of the death of her childhood coach Jaspal Rana in June.The skeet shooters, however, ensured India did not leave the shooting range empty-handed.The men's and women's teams both won bronze medals.Raiza Dhillon, Maheshwari Chauhan and Parinaaz Dhaliwal combined for a score of 331 to finish third in the women's team event. China won gold with 357 points, while Kazakhstan took silver with 336.Raiza and Parinaaz also reached the individual finals but could not finish on the podium.In the men's event, Anantjeet Singh Naruka, veteran Mairaj Ahmad Khan and Bhavtegh Singh Gill secured bronze with a combined score of 346.Anantjeet was the only Indian from the trio to reach the individual final and finished fourth.Wushu: Roshibina enters gold medal clashRoshibina Devi Naorem moved into the gold medal match in the women's 60kg category after defeating Indonesia's Thania Kusumaningtyas 2-0 at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall.She will face China's Xiaoyu Zhang in the final.Roshibina, 25, has already won a silver and a bronze medal in the previous two editions of the Asian Games.Badminton stars humbled by ChinaIndia's men's badminton team ended its campaign with a bronze medal after losing 1-3 to China in the semifinals.Lakshya Sen and Ayush Shetty could not get past their higher-ranked opponents, while Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty were the only Indians to win a match.India had won silver at the previous edition in Hangzhou in 2023, where China had also beaten them in the final.World No. 14 Lakshya, who had played a key role in India's run to the semifinals, lost 16-21, 18-21 to world No. 6 Shi Yu Qi in the opening singles match.India fell 0-1 behind, but Satwik and Chirag brought the team back into the contest.The Indian pair produced a strong performance to beat Paris Olympics silver medallists and reigning world champions Liang Wei Keng and Wang Chang 21-11, 22-20.However, Ayush Shetty and the second doubles pair of Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun could not win their matches as China sealed the tie.Table tennis, squash players move aheadIndian pairs Harmeet Desai-Yashaswini Ghorpade and Diya Chitale-Manush Shah advanced to the table tennis mixed doubles quarterfinals.The seventh-seeded Chitale and Shah made easy progress with a 3-0 win over the Sri Lanka-Maldives combination.In the round of 16, Shah and Chitale defeated Moosa Ahmed and Aishath Nazeem 11-0, 11-7, 11-6.They will face Hong Kong's Doo Hoi Kim and Wong Chun Ting in the quarterfinals on Thursday. A win will assure them of a medal.In squash, Abhay Singh, Veer Chotrani and Tanvi Khanna entered the round of 16 with comfortable victories.Second seed Abhay dropped only three points in his opening men's singles match against Thailand's Arkaradet Arkarahirunya, winning 11-1, 11-0, 11-2.Chotrani beat Sri Lanka's Shamil Wakeel 11-8, 11-3, 11-3 in the round of 32.In the women's singles, Tanvi defeated South Korea's Dami Kim 11-5, 11-7, 11-5.Women's hockey team continues winning runIndia's women's hockey team registered its third straight win in Pool B, thrashing Thailand 20-1.Drag-flicker Deepika Sehrawat was the star of the show, scoring a record nine goals in one match.Deepika scored in the 2nd, 8th, 9th, 24th, 33rd, 36th, 39th, 51st and 57th minutes. She converted all nine of her penalty-corner attempts.Navneet Kaur also scored four goals in the 4th, 29th, 35th and 51st minutes.India also continued its strong run in kabaddi, with both the men's and women's teams registering comprehensive wins over Bangladesh and Iran respectively in their group-stage matches.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who is Kate Martin? All about the Chicago Sky guard, her parents, ex-girlfriend and basketball journey
articles.summary: Kate Martin has continued her WNBA journey with the Chicago Sky after joining the team on a developmental contract in September 2026.
articles.body: Kate Martin has continued her WNBA journey with the Chicago Sky after joining the team on a developmental contract in September 2026. The former Iowa Hawkeyes star has already played for several teams since entering the league and is now looking to make the most of another opportunity.Martin was selected by the Las Vegas Aces in the 2024 WNBA Draft. She later played for the Golden State Valkyries and Los Angeles Sparks before joining Chicago. Away from basketball, Martin is also known for her close family connection to Iowa coach Jan Jensen and her previous relationship with fellow Iowa graduate Claire Gransee.Who is Kate Martin? Meet the Chicago Sky guardKate Martin is a professional basketball player from Moline, Illinois. She played college basketball for the Iowa Hawkeyes and became one of the team’s leaders during her time in Iowa City.Martin spent five seasons with Iowa and played 163 games. She was a team captain for four seasons. She also shared the court with Caitlin Clark during Iowa’s historic run to the NCAA championship game in 2023 and 2024.Her WNBA career began in 2024 when the Las Vegas Aces selected her with the 18th overall pick in the second round.Martin then became part of the Golden State Valkyries for their inaugural 2025 season after being selected in the expansion draft.She later joined the Los Angeles Sparks in 2026. During her time with the Sparks, she averaged 2.3 points in 7.1 minutes per game across 17 appearances.Martin also made history with the Sparks by becoming the first player in franchise history to move from a developmental contract to a standard roster deal.After being waived by Los Angeles, Martin joined the Chicago Sky on a developmental contract on September 2, 2026. She made her Sky debut against the Toronto Tempo and finished with five points and one assist.Her debut also had a special family connection.Iowa head coach Jan Jensen, who previously coached Martin, is her aunt. Jensen has remained one of Martin’s biggest supporters throughout her basketball career.Martin’s parents, Matt and Jill Martin, have also supported her throughout her basketball journey. They were among those celebrating when she was drafted by the Aces in 2024.Away from basketball, Martin’s personal life has also attracted attention.She was previously in a relationship with Claire Gransee, another University of Iowa graduate. The couple publicly confirmed their relationship in 2024.Gransee studied Communication Studies at Iowa and later worked in human resources. However, the pair are no longer together. Fans noticed that Martin removed references to Gransee from her social media in late 2025.Gransee has since moved on and publicly appeared in a relationship with NWSL goalkeeper Shelby Hogan.For Martin, the focus now remains on basketball. articles.summary: Brittney Griner’s relationship history has come under the spotlight as her divorce from Cherelle Griner moves through the courts.
articles.body: Brittney Griner’s relationship history has come under the spotlight as her divorce from Cherelle Griner moves through the courts. Cherelle has reportedly asked for continued financial support, citing a major difference between their incomes as the former couple works through their separation.Before her marriage to Cherelle, Brittney was briefly married to fellow WNBA player Glory Johnson. The former couple’s marriage lasted only weeks before Brittney sought an annulment. They later divorced and share twin daughters. Griner and Cherelle, meanwhile, married in 2018 and have a son together.Exploring Brittney Griner’s marriages to Glory Johnson and Cherelle GrinerAccording to the reported court documents, Cherelle has said there is a “substantial disparity” between her income and Griner’s. She also reportedly stated that she would be “unable to meet her reasonable financial needs on a monthly basis without continued support.”Griner currently plays for the Connecticut Sun. She signed a reported one-year contract worth $1.19 million. Cherelle works as a law clerk in Atlanta.The financial dispute comes after Griner filed for divorce on July 30, 2026. She listed July 24 as their separation date and described the marriage as “irretrievably broken.”Cherelle has also described the marriage as “irretrievably broken with no hope for reconciliation.” She is seeking joint custody of their son, Bash Raymond Griner. The divorce proceedings remain ongoing.The latest development has also brought attention to Griner’s previous marriage to Glory Johnson.Griner and Johnson, both professional basketball players, became engaged in 2014. In April 2015, they were arrested following a domestic dispute involving assault and disorderly conduct.Despite the incident, they married on May 8, 2015.The marriage was extremely short-lived. Just 28 days after the wedding, Griner filed for an annulment, citing fraud and duress. This came shortly after Johnson announced that she was pregnant with twins.The pair eventually divorced in June 2016. They share twin daughters.Griner later reconnected with Cherelle, whom she had first met while they were undergraduate students at Baylor University. The pair became romantically involved after Griner’s first marriage ended.They became one of the WNBA’s most visible couples. Cherelle supported Griner during some of the most difficult moments of her life.In 2022, Griner was detained in Russia after being arrested at a Moscow airport. She spent 10 months in Russian custody.Cherelle became a prominent public advocate for her release. She spoke publicly about Griner’s situation and met with President Joe Biden at the White House.Griner returned to the United States in December 2022 following a prisoner swap. The couple later appeared together at several major events, including the 2023 White House Correspondents Dinner and the Met Gala.In July 2024, Griner and Cherelle welcomed their son, Bash.Their relationship has since reached a different stage, with the divorce proceedings now focusing on custody and financial support. articles.title: 6 Cowboys players the Ravens must contain in Week 3 matchup in Brazil
articles.summary: Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and Quinnen Williams headline six Cowboys the Ravens must account for in their Week 3 game in Brazil
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens and Dallas Cowboys enter Week 3 in similar situations. Both teams sit at 1-1. Both believe they have enough talent to make noise this season. Both are looking to build momentum before the calendar flips to October.

The difference is how they arrived here. Dallas is coming off a confidence-building victory over the hated Washington Commanders , while Baltimore is still trying to digest a frustrating fourth-quarter collapse against the New Orleans Saints . The Ravens now travel to Rio de Janeiro knowing they cannot afford to let one loss turn into two.

If you've never been to Brazil, take this next statement as gospel. It's an easy place to lose focus. Make no mistake, though. These are professionals, and this is a business trip. If Baltimore expects to leave Brazil with a win, several Cowboys will need to be contained.

It's September, and we're nearing its end. October is approaching, which usually means one thing for opposing defenses: Dak Prescott is finding his groove and at his most dangerous. He enters this matchup fresh off one of the best performances of his season. He completed 26 of 31 passes for 279 yards and threw four touchdowns, leading Dallas to a 37-20 victory over Washington.

He also became the Cowboys' all-time leader in touchdown passes. Baltimore knows exactly what kind of challenge he presents. Prescott is at his best when he can operate comfortably from the pocket and distribute the football to his playmakers. If the Ravens allow him to settle in early, Dallas has enough weapons to create problems all afternoon.

CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , wide receivers

Few receiving duos are more dangerous than this one. CeeDee Lamb remains one of football's premier receivers and is coming off a huge performance against Washington, including 153 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Pickens complements him perfectly, giving Prescott another big-play option who can win contested catches downfield.

Together, they have 22 receptions, 265 yards, and three TDs this season (all by Lamb). Nate Wiggins, Marlon Humphrey and the rest of Baltimore's secondary will be tested from the opening kickoff . If Lamb and Pickens consistently win on the outside, the Ravens could find themselves chasing points again.

Not every game-changing player lines up on offense. Caleb Downs has wasted no time acclimating himself to the professional game. He has been everywhere through two weeks. He leads Dallas in tackles and has already shown a knack for creating momentum-changing plays.

Whether he's supporting the run defense or attacking the football, he has quickly become one of the Cowboys' most productive defenders. He leads all Cowboys defenders in total tackles (18 and solo tackles (11). He also has a sack, three forced fumbles, and a pass breakup through two games. Ball security will be a major emphasis for Baltimore this week, especially after mistakes proved costly against the Saints .

The Cowboys expected Donovan Ezeiruaku to make an impact. Few expected it to happen this quickly. He has been one of Dallas' most active defenders through two games, piling up tackles while making life difficult on opposing offenses.

Players like Ezeiruaku rarely receive the same attention as the stars, but they often become the reason drives stall. The Ravens already have enough self-inflicted wounds to clean up. They cannot allow Ezeiruaku to create additional ones.

A well-known star who was acquired in a trade with the New York Jets last season. He has amassed even total tackles this season, including one for loss. He has forced a fumble, but he is still looking for his first sack of the season.

It will come at some point. Ravens fans hope it doesn't come at Lamar Jackson 's expense. The key takeaway is that Quinnen Williams remains one of the NFL's most disruptive interior defenders, regardless of what the sack column says. He can wreck an offensive game plan in more ways than one. His ability to collapse the pocket and create chaos inside will test a Baltimore offensive line that has experienced some growing pains through two games.

Lamar Jackson's mobility can erase many mistakes. The Ravens would prefer not to test that theory repeatedly against Williams.

articles.title: 49ers signing veteran defender to help fill glaring need
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are very thin along their defensive line, so they're adding another veteran to the room to help out.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have taken some hits to their defensive line room early this season, with Mykel Williams on PUP and Alfred Collins out for the season on injured reserve.

With that in mind, the 49ers are bringing a veteran into the room, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported that they're signing Naquan Jones off the Minnesota Vikings practice squad.

Jones, 28, played at Michigan State from 2016-20. He went undrafted in 2021 and has had professional stints with the Tennessee Titans , Arizona Cardinals , Miami Dolphins , Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans .

In 60 professional games, he's recorded 102 tackles, 10 quarterback hits, 6.5 sacks and five passes defensed.

Jones should be a welcome addition to a rotation that will also include Osa Odighizuew, C.J. West and Gracen Halton. James Thompson Jr. is also in the room, but he suffered an injury on Sunday against the Dolphins.

articles.title: Wayne Rooney: “Livid” Man United legend threatens to sue ex-teammate over outrageous claim
articles.summary: 1Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney is reportedly threatening to take former England teammate Andy Carroll to court over a claim that they drank together...
articles.body:
Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney is reportedly threatening to take former England teammate Andy Carroll to court over a claim that they drank together while on England duty.

Carroll wrote in his new autobiography, 'Own It' , that Rooney would invite other England players into his room to smoke and drink while they were away with England.

Rooney earned 120 caps for England and was the nation's all-time leading goalscorer from September 2015, when he overtook Sir Bobby Charlton, until Harry Kane surpassed him.

Carroll claimed in his book about Rooney, "He'd be surrounded by cartons of fags, crates of lager and ­bottles of wine (which he got the hotel manager to deliver to his room), and soon his room would be full of players."

"No one got smashed, it was just Wazza's way of breaking the monotony with a couple of drinks."

United's record goalscorer responded that it was a "falsehood" and insisted that he and Carroll never truly socialised. He said that Carroll's claims were a "fabrication" and "disappointing."

Now, The Sun report that Rooney is weighing up taking the former Liverpool striker to court.

It is understood that Rooney sent a lawyers' letter to the publishers of Carroll's book demanding a retraction of the controversial claim.

The newspaper claims that a source told them, "Wayne is livid. He's not messing around."

"His legal team have sent a strongly worded letter to the publisher. He wants it retracted as it is completely untrue."

"Wayne knows he's no angel but this crossed the line. It's a matter of principle."

"Andy is spiralling over the whole situation. He didn't think for a second Rooney would kick off like this. Andy had a book to sell and now he's in over his head."

"There may be a public apology coming unless he wants a legal battle on his hands."

articles.title: Vote for the Journal Sentinel's play of the week for the week of Sept. 14
articles.summary: Vote from four nominees for what you think is the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel's high school play of the week for the week of Sept. 14-19, 2026.
articles.body:
What was the best play in the Milwaukee area this past week? You tell us.

This past week featured four excellent plays from Week 5 action of high school football around the area and you can decide by voting for the best one from now until noon on Saturday, Sept. 26, as many times as you'd like.

We now have a submission tool on our Preps Plus portion of the Journal Sentinel website. The location to upload your clips is under the top banner that's labeled " Upload Your Video ". It's a four-step process that will allow you to upload clips from the week across all fall sports. The clips must be trimmed and uploaded to be 30 seconds or shorter in the proper formatting to be eligible for selection. Please submit your clips by the end of the day on Mondays to make sure your clip is potentially included to be a nominee.

If you have any questions about submitting a play of the week nominee, contact Michael Whitlow via email at mwhitlow@gannett.com.

Port Washington football vs. West Bend West on Sept. 18

Mason Schwanz, sr., Port Washington: Schwanz ran 15 times for 65 yards with two crucial touchdowns in the fourth quarter of Port Washington's 20-12 win over West Bend West in the rain on Friday, Sept. 18. On the first of his two short-yardage scores, he and quarterback Jack Bunyan worked together to save the play with Schwanz falling into the end zone to give the Pirates a 13-12 advantage they wouldn't relinquish.

Larry McCain, sr., Milwaukee Bay View: On top of his duties as a linebacker for the Bay View defense, Redcats quarterback Larry McCain does it all for the offense, too. In Bay View's first victory over Pulaski in nine seasons to capture the Wooden Football on Thursday, Sept. 17, McCain scored on the ground three times, including this 36-yarder to give the Redcats a 12-0 lead in a 20-12 win for Bay View.

Elex Mentch, jr., West Bend West: Mentch touched the ball three times in West Bend West's 20-12 loss to Port Washington and this one was his most important carry. On fourth-and-5 in the early moments of the fourth quarter with Port leading 7-6, Mentch took the reverse, shook off a few Port defenders and found himself in the end zone with a 25-yard score to give the Spartans a 12-7 lead.

Mace Miskel, jr., Whitefish Bay: Week 5 was seemingly the Mace Miskel game for the Whitefish Bay Blue Dukes in their 35-14 win over Slinger on Friday, Sept. 18. Miskel scored three times (49, 69, 78 yards) on three offensive touches and intercepted a pass on defense for the Blue Dukes in the victory, including the 78-yard catch-and-run in the video above.

articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals stud cornerback Will Johnson has shown flashes throughout his young NFL career, but injuries have hindered him from reaching his full potential. Johnson missed five games in his rookie season due to an early-season groin injury and a back/hip injury in early November. articles.title: Bears QB Crisis Hits New Level After Ben Johnson’s Latest Admission
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears entered the week expecting Tyson Bagent to take over for Caleb Williams. By Wednesday, even that plan […]
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears entered the week expecting Tyson Bagent to take over for Caleb Williams . By Wednesday, even that plan was no longer certain.

Williams is dealing with a right hamstring injury and has not practiced this week. Bagent, who replaced Williams late in Sunday's loss to Minnesota , is now in the NFL's concussion protocol . That leaves 38-year-old Case Keenum as the only active Bears quarterback practicing. Yet, coach Ben Johnson still refuses to name him the starter for Monday night's game against the Philadelphia Eagles .

"We're at a point right now [where we're] not sure who the starter's going to be on Monday night," Johnson said Wednesday.

That is not the sentence Chicago wanted to hear four days before a prime-time game against one of the NFC's strongest teams.

The Bears' quarterback situation has changed almost by the hour. Williams suffered the hamstring injury during a non-contact scramble in the fourth quarter of the 9-3 loss to Minnesota. Johnson has described the injury as week-to-week, and Williams is not expected to practice before Monday.

Preseason star Bagent appeared to be the obvious replacement until he entered concussion protocol Tuesday. He completed five of nine passes for 54 yards after taking over against the Vikings, leading Chicago on a late drive that reached the Minnesota 12-yard line before the offense stalled. Now Bagent's availability depends on clearing the league's five-step return-to-play process. He was not at Halas Hall Wednesday, while Williams participated only in the team's walk-through.

That left Keenum taking the practice reps. "We know Case is the one that's practicing today," Johnson said. "So we'll figure it out as we go."

Keenum has 66 career starts and has played for nine NFL teams. Unfortunately, he has not thrown a regular-season pass since 2023. His role with Chicago has primarily been as a veteran mentor to Williams and Bagent. Johnson, however, insists Keenum is not some emergency option who has been sitting around collecting dust.

"He's at the point of his career where he's like another coach in a lot of ways," Johnson said. "He's seen a ton. He knows what good football looks like. He knows what a healthy locker room looks like, and he's a key part of what we do."

That experience is valuable, but it does not erase the reality of the matchup. The Eagles are coming to Soldier Field on Monday night, and Chicago's offense is already trying to recover from a three-point performance against Minnesota after scoring 59 in the opener.

The Bears also will not add another quarterback this week, according to Johnson. If Williams and Bagent remain unavailable, undrafted rookie Miller Moss would likely be elevated from the practice squad to serve as Keenum's backup.

Johnson praised general manager Ryan Poles for building a quarterback room with three players he believes can win games.

"We've got three guys that can play ball in this league, that have won games in this league," Johnson said.

That confidence is important, but the uncertainty is impossible to hide. Chicago is preparing for Philadelphia without knowing whether its starter will be an injured franchise quarterback, a backup trying to clear concussion protocol or a 38-year-old veteran making his first regular-season appearance in nearly three years.

The Bears can call it business as usual . It is anything but.

articles.title: Alex Afari on journey back to Kentucky: 'I just wanted to play'
articles.summary: Alex Afari Jr. is back for a fifth season with Kentucky's football. He met with reporters Wednesday for the first time since he rejoined the Wildcats.
articles.body:
LEXINGTON — In July, as Alex Afari Jr. started to see more players in his situation — Class of 2022 high school graduates who weren't granted a fifth year of eligibility by the NCAA — return to college, he began to believe a Kentucky comeback was possible. So, after hiring an attorney, Afari became a party in a successful injunction in Jefferson Circuit Court last month.

"It felt great, because I just wanted to play," said Afari, who spoke with media members Wednesday, Sept. 23, in his first media availability since rejoining the Wildcats . "I felt like last year I didn't really finish how I wanted to."

"I wanted to come back," Afari said. "And when I knew I could come back, I had all the emotions. It just hit me."

Afari practiced during preseason camp following the injunction. But an appeal put that ruling on hold. As a result, UK and coach Will Stein sidelined Afari until the situation resolved itself.

"It was playing with my heart a little bit," Afari said of the stop-and-go nature of his eligibility saga. "But it felt good when I was able to come back and just practice."

Unlike other members of the 2022 graduating class who were granted a fifth year and sought to find a new school, Afari said leaving UK never crossed his mind.

"It was always coming back to Kentucky . I knew this is where I started, and this is where I wanted to finish," he said. "I didn't want to go nowhere else. When I was coming here to train and do some treatments and stuff like that, I (saw) the coaches and how bought-in the players (were) in the program and just how different it was.

"That made me want to come back and play here."

Kentucky Wildcats play Texas A&M Aggies. See photos from the game

After also not recording any stats in the loss to Alabama , Afari got on the board in last week's upset of Texas A&M , collecting two tackles and a pass breakup. He admitted he's still learning defensive coordinator Jay Bateman 's scheme.

"I think I'm just gonna hone in on one spot right now, just to learn one spot. It's a lot of defense — a lot," Afari said. "But it's good. ... When I get more comfortable at that spot, (they) can move me around."

Originally from Ghana, Afari has appeared in 51 games in five seasons with the Cats.

After missing out on the postseason the past two years, Afari aims to get the program back on the right track.

"I wanted to come back to this place," he said, "and finish it right."

articles.title: Lions gearing up for chess match vs. familiar Aaron Glenn-led defense
articles.summary: Aaron Glenn, now head coach of the New York Jets, spent four years as defensive coordinator with the Detroit Lions.
articles.body:
ALLEN PARK — The Detroit Lions know Aaron Glenn.

And the Lions know Glenn knows, and Glenn knows the Lions know.

For the first time since he left to become a head coach, Glenn will return to Ford Field, this time as an opponent, when his New York Jets play the Lions on Sunday, Sept. 27. Glenn, who spent four seasons as Detroit 's defensive coordinator, is intimately familiar with the Lions, and vise versa.

"There's things that he knows we want to hang our hat on," Lions coach Dan Campbell said Wednesday, Sept. 23. "I mean, that's just gonna be there. And (there's) things that I know that he wants to hang his hat on. ... But then there'll be these other things. Because we know that, he knows that, there'll be these wrinkles that get thrown in. It'll be everything from a front to a pressure to a third down, you get a couple of these other looks that they haven't put on tape yet."

Campbell and Glenn were together on the same coaching staff each year from 2016-24, first overlapping with the New Orleans Saints (2016-20) before Campbell in 2021 was hired to lead the Lions and brought Glenn with him to coordinate the defense.

There were lows during Glenn's time with the Lions. But Campbell stuck by him, culminating in Detroit's defense ranking seventh in points allowed in 2024 (20.1), when the team won a franchise-record 15 contests before losing to the Washington Commanders in the divisional round.

"When things go well, that's one thing," Campbell said of why he never wavered on Glenn. "When things get a little rocky, that's where you really find out what your conviction in something is, and in someone. Solving issues, confidence in themselves, the ability to teach, the response from the players. When you check all the boxes, even if things don't always look the way you want them to look, you don't just let go of good coaches. ... You've got to look through all the other stuff and really look at the substance behind it."

The Jets struggled in Glenn's first season but have been strong on defense through two games in 2026, including a Week 1 win over the Tennessee Titans and an overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2. They rank first in average yards allowed per game (197), seventh in average points allowed (15) and are tied for fourth in EPA allowed per play (-0.25).

Lions associate head coach and wide receivers coach Scottie Montgomery pointed out the influence he sees from Brian Duker, who is in his first year as defensive coordinator with the Jets and was previously with the Lions as an assistant under Campbell and Glenn from 2021-23.

"There's a lot that we know, but there is evolution on both sides. ... So, now we're in a situation to where we've got to deal with a little bit of what we know, and then the unknown," Montgomery said of Glenn's defense. "Looking at the way the first two games went, you can definitely see the uptick in this team, whether it be not only because of talent, but scheme fitting together, their talent being in good situations.

"He uses their secondary in some very manipulative ways, playing a lot more two-shell than we've seen him play. But also on third down, not being afraid to come play you in man-to-man coverage so that when you do get in those situations, he does have some unpredictability there, like a lot of other teams that we've faced."

Asked about the potential for this being a trap game (the Lions are favored by 6½ points), Campbell pushed back, not only pointing to his team's loss to the Buffalo Bills on Sept. 17, but also its understanding of the type of effort a Glenn-led defense can produce.

"Our players know exactly what's coming in here because the defensive coordinator was here for (four) years," Campbell said. "Turn on the tape. ... This is gonna be a knockout, 60-minute brawl. It's gonna go down, and we've got to be on point. We can't beat ourselves, we've got to make the plays that are there, and everybody's got to do their job. I don't see that (as a trap game), and our players, I can't imagine they see that."

▶ Kickoff: 1 p.m. Sunday, Ford Field, Detroit, Michigan

▶ Series: Detroit leads, 8-7 (Last meeting: Lions won, 20-17, on Dec. 18, 2022 in East Rutherford, New Jersey )

Arsenal have agreed a deal to keep Mikel Arteta as their manager for the long term , and the Gunners will continue looking for ways to keep their successful team intact.

Without the former midfielder, the project could face significant disruption, and Arsenal do not want to become too comfortable in assuming that Arteta will never consider leaving the club.

Giving Arteta a new contract is not the only step Arsenal have taken to keep the manager satisfied. According to Give Me Sport , the Gunners have also secured new deals for all of his assistants.

Arteta's coaching staff have played an important role in helping the manager develop the team, while their work has contributed to the continued growth of the squad.

Keeping the group together was therefore another priority for Arsenal, particularly as the club looks to maintain their progress and continue competing at the highest level.

The new agreements mean Arteta will continue working alongside the assistants who have supported him throughout his time at the club, providing further continuity behind the scenes.

Arteta is likely to be pleased with the decision to keep his coaching staff together, given how important each member has been to the development of his team.

The manager knows that maintaining a strong group around him can help Arsenal continue building on their progress, while the club also recognise the importance of providing stability to the project.

With Arteta committed to a new long-term deal and his assistants also secured, Arsenal have taken further steps towards maintaining the structure that has helped the team develop.

articles.title: Olympic champ Alysa Liu stuns in British Vogue photos amid skating hiatus
articles.summary: United States star figure skater Alysa Liu stole the show in a new photoshoot with British Vogue this week.
articles.body:
United States star figure skater two-time Olympic champion Alysa Liu is in the midst of a figure skating hiatus, but that doesn't mean she's not busy.

Liu, who won two gold medals at the 2026 Milan Cortina Games , announced earlier this summer that she'd be taking a break from competition.

"While people are announcing programs, imma take this time to announce that I will not be competing this season. I always want to challenge myself in new ways, so my artistry & skating can evolve," she said in a statement at the time. "It's important to me that my sport reflects my personal growth. I'm gonna take the time to recalibrate, fine-tune things & whatnot. So fear not, I'll be back, & in the meantime I'll be rooting for my teammates near & far."

In the midst of her break, Liu is staying busy.

As she takes a break from her profession, Liu posed for British Vogue and revealed the intentions behind her hiatus from the skating world.

"It's important to do things on my own terms, because for so long I didn't," she explains. "I need to be able to control it creatively, otherwise I'd rather not do it at all."

Liu mused that photoshoots are similar to skating program in her head "because all of it needs to tell a story."

It's art," said Liu . "I feel like when I'm being heard, I can put my all into it because I'm more comfortable."

The star skater did not put a timeline on her return to the ice.

articles.title: Freshman Tim Ibukunoluwa brings 'relentless' style of play from Australia to Siena basketball
articles.summary: Siena coach Nevada Smith, who's not shy about setting high expectations for his players, said Ibukunoluwa could be the best rebounder in the Metro Conference...
articles.body:
LOUDONVILLE - To end the first day of practice , Siena men's basketball freshman Tim Ibukunoluwa received a pass at halfcourt, took one dribble and found teammate Reid Ducharme cutting down the left wing for a reverse layup.

Ibukunoluwa and Ducharme jumped and bumped chests to celebrate the basket that lifted the white team over the green team in a scrimmage on the final play of Tuesday's workout.

"Especially after (we) probably didn't have the best practice as the white team, missing a couple bunnies, but feel like that was really good to get that one in the end," Ibukunoluwa said.

Ibukunoluwa, a 6-foot-8, 215-pound Australian, was impressive in the final half-hour that was open to the media. He grabbed several offensive rebounds, including a follow-up dunk, and also passed to classmate Parrish Edmond Jr. for a slam.

"Yeah, Tim's an animal," graduate guard Brendan Coyle said. "He can play pretty much wherever you want him to. Step out and hit a 3, and he rebounds like a madman. You know, Tim kind of does a little bit of everything, and it's been really great to see."

Siena coach Nevada Smith, who's not shy about setting high expectations for his players, said Ibukunoluwa could be the best rebounder in the Metro Conference this season. He has a 6-foot-11 wingspan.

"His effort is relentless," Smith said. "He's going to rebound the ball at a high rate. I don't know if there's a better rebounder in our league than him. It'll be interesting to see. I personally think he's the best."

Smith also praised Ibukunoluwa's versatility. He said the freshman will sometimes be the biggest player on the court for the Saints but can also make plays with the ball in his hands.

Ibukunoluwa said he learned those guard skills before he had his growth spurt. He also got sound advice from his two older brothers - Josh, who is a 6-foot-10, 230-pound junior forward at Bradley University, and John, who played at Division II West Virginia Wesleyan.

They're the sons of Nigerian parents who moved to Perth, Australia, for job opportunities.

"They've seen how the game's evolving and they told me early, you've got to be able to play at both ends of the court, defense and offense, and guard 1 (point guard) through 5 (center)," Tim Ibukunoluwa said.

He spent the past two years playing for the Willeton Tigers in NBL1, which is Australia's top semiprofessional league. He moved to Canada last winter to compete for Orangeville Prep in Ontario, the same path that Josh Ibukunoluwa took.

"More exposure to scouts and just getting set into the college mindset," Tim Ibukunoluwa explained.

He discovered Siena through an Australian teammate whose management put him in touch with Saints assistant Matt Blue, who previously coached at the NBA Global Academy in Australia.

He did his homework on Siena, which won the Metro Conference under former coach Gerry McNamara.

"I didn't know much about Siena, but after my research, I saw what they did last year, obviously, with G-Mac and what they did this year. Nevada was, like, a really good coach, has great history and all the other coaches do as well," Ibukunoluwa said.

He chose Siena after also looking at Radford and Bowling Green.

"I just thought I'd get the most playing time here," he said. "The culture here is very good as well. They were very nice to my family."

Ibukunoluwa said he always wanted to play college basketball in the United States because "this is the spot." His brother Josh has advised him to adjust to the American game by being very assertive and not losing confidence in his game.

"I feel like that's just a big part of my game, my motor," Tim Ibukunoluwa said. "I'm just going to keep on going. Nothing's going to stop me from rebounding the ball."

articles.title: Lions Coach Says Isaac TeSlaa’s Opportunities Will Be Limited
articles.summary: Lions receivers coach Scottie Montgomery says Isaac TeSlaa's opportunities will stay limited behind St. Brown and Williams. #Lions
articles.body:
Through the first two games of the 2026 NFL season, Detroit Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa has caught just two passes for 26 yards and no touchdowns. He is averaging 13.0 yards per reception on six targets.

TeSlaa will need to produce more as the third wide receiver in the Lions offense at some point this season. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams are the top two options in Detroit's passing game. With the Week 3 matchup against the New York Jets approaching, Lions wide receivers coach Scottie Montgomery spoke to the media Wednesday about TeSlaa's lack of production through the first two weeks.

Scottie Montgomery Reveals a Harsh Truth About Isaac TeSlaa

Detroit sports reporter Brad Galli covered the Lions press conference on Wednesday and relayed what Montgomery said about TeSlaa's role moving forward.

According to Galli , Montgomery said TeSlaa's "opportunities are going to be limited." Montgomery added that the Lions' first and second progressions have been open, so TeSlaa's main chances will come in "pressure situations" on fourth down and in the red zone.

What Would Open Up More Targets for Isaac TeSlaa

That leaves the clearest path to more targets running through an injury to St. Brown, Williams or Sam LaPorta, which nobody in Detroit wants. Even so, giving TeSlaa a bigger role as the third option could make the offense harder to defend. Montgomery's comments have not gone over well with a portion of the Lions fan base.

articles.title: Bengals get bad news as 400-plus yard WR is headed to IR amid thumb injury
articles.summary: This is a tough blow for the Bengals' offense after Week 2.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals are 2-0 to begin the 2026 NFL Season, with wins over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Houston Texans . Their defense has looked great, and the offense, led by Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase at wide receiver, looks strong.

However, the Bengals, following their Week 2 victory, have lost a key receiver. While Higgins and Chase are fine, their No. 3 WR has been lost for some time.

Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic is reporting that the Bengals' Andrei Iosivas is headed for injured reserve and will miss at least four weeks due to a thumb injury.

Bengals get bad news on Andrei Iosivas amid IR report

"Andrei Iosivas tore a ligament in his thumb and is going on IR," Dehner reports. "It will not end his season, according to Zac Taylor."

This is an unfortunate blow for the Bengals offense, as Iosivas has been a productive receiver the past two seasons for Cincinnati.

In 2024, Iosivas caught 36 of his 61 targets for 279 yards and six touchdowns. Last season, he caught 33 of 58 targets for 435 yards and two touchdowns.

While he's been the team's No. 3 receiver the past few years, Iosivas is a quality depth option who has over 1,000 yards and 12 touchdowns in his NFL career.

Now that he's landing on IR, Iosivas is going to miss the next four weeks at minimum, meaning he'll miss Weeks 3, 4, 5, and 7 due to the Week 6 bye for Cincinnati.

The mention from Taylor that this isn't a season-ending issue, however, indicates this IR stay might be longer than four weeks for Iosivas.

Taking his place on the WR depth chart will be a combination of two intriguing young WRs. Colbie Young , the 24-year-old rookie out of Georgia, and 26-year-old Dohnte Meyers will factor into the WR room as depth options.

Joe Burrow still has his top targets to throw to in Higgins and Chase, and tight ends Mike Gesicki and Erick All Jr. should see their fair share of work.

The Bengals will be without Iosivas for an extended period of time. He's slated to miss at least four weeks, and this thumb injury appears to be more serious, so more than four weeks could be on the table for the Bengals ' fourth-year WR.

articles.title: Jets WR Arian Smith has season-ending ACL injury and DL David Onyemata out after core muscle surgery
articles.summary: New York Jets wide receiver Arian Smith is out for the season after needing surgery to repair a torn ACL in one of his knees.  Smith, a fourth-round pick in...
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. (AP) — New York Jets wide receiver Arian Smith is out for the season after needing surgery to repair a torn ACL in one of his knees.

Smith, a fourth-round pick in last year's draft, was placed on the injured reserve list Tuesday and coach Aaron Glenn announced Wednesday that the speedy receiver will not return this season.

"Tough," Glenn said. "But he'll bounce back very well."

Defensive tackle David Onyemata will be sidelined several weeks after Glenn said he had core muscle surgery. Onyemata, also on IR, could return before the end of the season, according to Glenn.

Both players were injured in the Jets' 20-17 overtime loss to Green Bay last Sunday.

Smith had no catches in the first two games and had just one target — a dropped pass in the opener at Tennessee . He struggled with consistency as a rookie last season, finishing with just seven catches for 52 yards on 16 targets in 16 games.

The former Georgia standout, who had issues with drops at times in college, has outstanding speed and was considered a potential vertical threat for Frank Reich's offense.

The Jets signed undrafted rookie Malik McClain from the practice squad to help fill Smith's role.

Onyemata signed a one-year, $10.5 million contract with the Jets in March, reuniting him Glenn. The two were together in New Orleans from 2016 through the 2020 seasons when Glenn was the Saints' defensive backs coach.

The 34-year-old Onyemata had yet to make much of an impact for New York, registering a quarterback hit and no tackles in the first two games. His absence will likely mean increased snaps for Jowon Briggs and rookie fourth-rounder Darrell Jackson Jr. on the D-line.

Mason Taylor is among several players sitting out practice with injuries

The Jets (1-1) are dealing with several other injuries as they prepare to face the Lions (1-1) in Detroit on Sunday.

Tight end Mason Taylor (thumb), safety Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin), linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps) and running back/kick returner Kene Nwangwu (back) were all expected to sit out practice, Glenn said.

Taylor was injured late in the loss to the Packers , but Glenn insisted "he'll be just fine."

Edge rusher Joseph Ossai is still recovering from a ruptured plantar fascia in his left foot suffered during the preseason finale against the Giants on Aug. 28. He was being listed as limited at practice Wednesday.

"Very close," Glenn said of Ossai's chances of making his Jets debut. "So we'll see how that actually operates during the week."

Rookie edge rusher David Bailey, the No. 2 overall pick in April who has a sack in each of his first two NFL games, was also expected to be limited with an elbow ailment that Glenn wasn't concerned about.

Will Levis makes his practice debut with the Jets

Former Titans quarterback Will Levis practiced with the Jets for the first time since being signed to the practice squad on Tuesday.

The 27-year-old Levis was released by the Titans last month and is working behind starter Geno Smith and rookie Cade Kubnik, a fourth-rounder, as the third-string quarterback.

"A good player that we feel like we can develop," Glenn said. "He'll be on our practice squad, he'll get reps against our defense."

Levis went 5-16 as a starter in Tennessee with 3,899 yards passing, 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions after being a second-round pick in 2023.

"It's a good move to get a player like that," Glenn said, "to be a part of what we're trying to build."

articles.title: Braves Reinstate Two-Time All-Star Pitcher From Injured List Just In Time For Postseason
articles.summary: Robert Suárez is back from the 60-day injured list
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves signed Robert Suárez to a three-year, $45 million deal last offseason, but he has been on the injured list since June 23.

Suárez was dealing with right elbow inflammation and just finished his rehab assignment. The Braves announced on Wednesday that they are reinstating him from the injured list. Suárez being back set the Braves' bullpen up nicely for the postseason.

Suárez had a 0.56 ERA in 31 games before his injury. He had a strong case to be an All-Star, but unlike the last two years in San Diego , the Braves were not using him as their closer. They had Raisel Iglesias in that role after they also re-signed him. Together, Iglesias and Suàrez are one of the best bullpen tandems in baseball and can dominate teams for the final six outs of a game.

The Braves starting rotation has some question marks for October, but having Suárez and Iglesias both healthy shortens the bridge between the starter and closing the game. Both right-handers are closers, and having to face one of them in the eighth inning is a nightmare for teams.

Suárez made just one outing for Triple-A Gwinnett during his rehab assignment. He pitched a scoreless inning with one strikeout, needing just 11 pitches. The Braves will most likely be playing a Wild Card Series starting Tuesday, and Suárez will no doubt be on the roster for that. The Braves will likely get him some action in the big leagues in their final five games.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo sets ambitious Portugal national team targets ahead of ‘new era’
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has set ambitious targets for both himself and the Portuguese national team ahead of their UEFA Nations League title defense kickoff agains...
articles.body:
Five-time Ballon d'Or winner Cristiano Ronaldo is well and truly on the back nine of his storied career, with the 41-year-old preparing to make his 234th appearance for the Portuguese national team .

With his sixth and final FIFA World Cup now behind him, and with Portugal having failed to make it past the Round of 16, where they lost to eventual champions Spain , Al-Nassr forward Ronaldo has been called up once more by new national team boss Jorge Jesus.

A coach Ronaldo is well acquainted with, with Jesus having guided Al-Nassr to the Manchester United and Real Madrid legend's first Saudi Pro League title last season, he is confident that both he and the team can achieve big things under the leadership of the 72-year-old.

"My objective is twofold: goal number 1000 and winning the [UEFA] Nations League," Ronaldo declared ahead of their first of four games this international window, stating that they are entering "a new era," as per Marca .

He went on to add that Jesus "was a perfect choice" to replace Roberto Martínez as head coach following the World Cup, explaining, "He brings a different atmosphere, different ideas and a different language. As the coach said, many have already worked with him, which makes things easier."

Ronaldo also addressed his critics who believe it's time for him to close the chapter on his national team career, commenting, "I can't be completely honest... I have to be politically correct. Something I usually say is that I have always been very well received, but this was one of the years in which I felt the most affection. I understand that there are some media outlets trying to kill me, but only with a shotgun. And even so, I dodge the bullet."

Despite his critics, Ronaldo remains as confident in himself and his abilities as ever, stating, "I believe I make it to the national team because I make the difference at my club.

"I'm available for whatever the coach needs, whether that's to play, come on as a substitute, or not play... I know the coach is counting on me, and I'm not here because of my résumé, but because of what I do at my club."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

So far this season, having worked his way slowly back into the Al-Nassr lineup after an extended summer break, Ronaldo has found the back of the net three times in seven games under new head coach Ange Postecoglou. Entering the international window, the defending champions sit third in the league standings with 16 points after seven games, two points behind leaders Al-Hilal.

Having turned 41 in February, exactly how much longer Ronaldo intends to play remains up in the air, commenting that he is simply 'living in the moment' and that "it is very possible that this will be his last year."

As for his national team career, Ronaldo stated that "when I feel that I'm not doing anything, I'll pack my bags. I only think about the present... I know many people want me to leave now, but my motivation comes from the people who still want to see me."

Currently chasing his 1,000th career goal, and the 147th of his national team career, Ronaldo's next opportunity to close the gap on this ambitious target will come on Thursday when they host Wales in the Nations League - looking to kick off their title defense in fashion at Estádio José Alvalade.

This will be followed by a trip to take on Norway on Sunday, before they continue their road trip in Denmark on October 1. Finally, they'll close out this window back on home soil against Norway on October 4.

articles.title: Última hora de Santa Marta por el paro armado de 'Los Pachenca': Turistas atrapados, comercio cerrado y militarización
articles.standfirst: Caos y terror en Santa Marta por el paro armado: Calles desoladas y turistas atrapados por el paro armado de 'Los Pachenca'
articles.summary: Caos y terror en Santa Marta por el paro armado: Calles desoladas y turistas atrapados por el paro armado de 'Los Pachenca'
articles.body: La capital del departamento del Magdalena amaneció sumida en un ambiente de profunda tensión, zozobra y baja actividad comercial. Tras la amenaza de un paro armado de 48 horas decretado por las Autodefensas Conquistadoras de la Sierra Nevada (ACSN) —conocidas popularmente como Los Pachenca—, la ciudad turística ha registrado cierres parciales de establecimientos, afectaciones en el transporte y a cientos de visitantes atrapados en hoteles y playas. La escalada de violencia y la posterior parálisis de la zona costera se desencadenaron tras un operativo de las fuerzas de seguridad llevado a cabo el lunes 21 de septiembre. En dicho operativo cayó abatido José Luis Pérez Villanueva, alias Cholo, quien era señalado por las autoridades como el segundo cabecilla en la estructura de mando de Los Pachenca. En respuesta a la muerte de alias Cholo, el grupo armado emitió un panfleto intimidatorio decretando una restricción total de actividades y movilidad por 48 horas en Santa Marta, la carretera Troncal del Caribe, el municipio de Ciénaga y otros sectores aledaños del departamento del Magdalena. Durante la jornada del martes 22 de septiembre, integrantes armados pertenecientes presuntamente a las ACSN comenzaron a hacer cumplir la amenaza por la fuerza: Uno de los sectores más castigados por esta crisis ha sido el del turismo, motor económico de la región. En emblemáticos puntos de la ciudad como El Rodadero y las rutas que conducen hacia Playa Blanca o el Parque Nacional Natural Tayrona, la actividad quedó completamente suspendida. Arnulfo Cuervo, presidente de la Federación Colombiana de Transportadores de Carga (Fedetranscarga), confirmó que la paralización de los despachos de mercancía impactó fuertemente la economía local y regional: Pérdidas en Santa Marta: Se calcula un perjuicio económico de 39.000 millones de pesos en el primer día de paro. Impacto regional: En el conjunto de la región Caribe, el impacto ascendió a los 42.000 millones de pesos. Empleos en riesgo: En el departamento del Magdalena, alrededor de 26.000 personas dependen directamente del transporte de carga. Sumando las actividades conexas de comercio y turismo, cerca de 120.000 empleos se ven amenazados por la parálisis. Por su parte, Nidia Hernández, presidenta de la Federación Colombiana de Transportadores de Carga por Carretera (Colfecar), denunció el deterioro del orden público y el asedio constante contra los conductores y la infraestructura de transporte. "Cada vez que los grupos armados sienten la presión del Ejército y la Policía, salen a desquitarse con los transportadores. Han incinerado vehículos y existen amenazas directas contra los parqueaderos donde permanecen estacionadas las tractomulas", advirtió Hernández. Ante la gravedad de los hechos, las asociaciones gremiales adelantan coordinaciones bajo reserva con la Fuerza Pública para implementar esquemas de protección y caravanas que garanticen la movilidad sin arriesgar la vida de los conductores. Ante la gravedad de los acontecimientos, las autoridades nacionales y locales ordenaron una intervención de gran escala: Las máximas autoridades de la región y el Gobierno Nacional realizaron un consejo de seguridad extraordinario en la ciudad para coordinar el plan de choque y hacer presencia institucional en puntos clave como la plaza de mercado y barrios populares. articles.title: Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris Eligible for 2027 UFL Season After LSU, NFL Roster Saga
articles.summary: Former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris have at least one pathway to play professionally after getting stuck in a career limbo.
articles.body:
Former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris have at least one pathway to play professionally after getting stuck in a career limbo.

Amanda Christovich and Mark Maske of Front Office Sports reported Wednesday the pair are eligible to join the UFL. Their interest in taking part in the league is unknown, though.

Wright and Harris both signed with NFL teams this spring after going undrafted. However, they sought a return to the college game once the NCAA amended its eligibility rules. Athletes are now permitted to play five seasons within a five-year window.

LSU coach Lane Kiffin attempted to bring his former Rebels players with him to Baton Rouge. Their status remained up in the air as the season was kicking off, and it was only after the Tigers' 51-10 win that school president Wade Rousse confirmed Kiffin had dropped the idea.

On Sept. 16, The Ringer's Tom Pelissero shared a memo from the NFL outlining that Wright and Harris were also prohibited from returning during the current season:

The UFL has the flexibility to make its own rulings on player eligibility. Back in June, league co-owner Mike Repole made overtures to former Cincinnati and Texas Tech quarterback Brendan Sorsby after he got stuck in a similar one-year purgatory.

Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton asserted this summer the UFL can be a pathway for aspiring NFL players to sharpen their game. Defensive back Sean Fresch Jr. is signed to Denver's practice squad after playing in the UFL in 2025 and 2026.

For Wright and Harris, this would present an opportunity to shake off some rust before they try to revive their NFL careers. They may decide it's not worth it given the risk of injury and how much of the UFL season overlaps with offseason NFL workouts.

articles.title: Christian Eriksen Agrees To Terminate Wolfsburg Contract After June On-Field Collapse
articles.summary: Christian Eriksen has agreed to terminate his contract with German soccer club Wolfsburg, nearly four months after the Danish midfielder collapsed on the field for the second time in his career, the team said Wednesday.
articles.body: Christian Eriksen has agreed to terminate his contract with German soccer club Wolfsburg, nearly four months after the Danish midfielder collapsed on the field for the second time in his career, the team said Wednesday. The 34-year-old Eriksen hasn't played since he collapsed after clutching his chest during Denmark’s friendly match against Ukraine in Odense, Denmark on June 7. His contract had been due to run until the end of June 2027. "At the moment, it is important for me to be close to my family in Denmark. I’m pleased that we were able to find a solution together," Eriksen said in a statement issued by the club. "It was a great pleasure for me to play for you, and I will look back fondly on this period." The incident in June brought back memories of Eriksen's cardiac arrest at the European Championship five years earlier, as players formed a circle around him while he received medical attention. He was able to walk off the field by himself and was taken to a hospital. Eriksen said in June he was "doing well" and that an implantable cardioverter defibrillator fitted to support his heart after the 2021 incident had done its job. He had been undergoing rehabilitation in Denmark since. The former Manchester United and Tottenham player had joined Wolfsburg as a free agent before the 2025-26 season, which ended with the team being relegated from the Bundesliga. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Case Keenum Practices For Bears Amid Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent Uncertainty
articles.summary: It looks as if Case Keenum is going to start at quarterback for the Chicago Bears on Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body: It looks as if Case Keenum is going to start at quarterback for the Chicago Bears on Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles. Tyson Bagent and Caleb Williams are two more possibilities, depending on their health. When it comes to the QBs for the Bears, very little is certain at the moment. The 38-year-old Keenum practiced on Wednesday as Chicago ramped up its preparation for its matchup with Philadelphia. Keenum hasn't played in a regular-season game since Dec. 24, 2023, but at least he is healthy right now. "We feel really good about whoever ends up playing for us and that showed in the preseason, shows up in practice every single day," coach Ben Johnson said. "So we’re at a point right now, not sure who the starter is going to be on Monday night. We’ll let this thing play out, and we’ll go from there." Williams left Sunday’s 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings with a right hamstring injury after he got hurt on a scramble midway through the fourth quarter. The No. 1 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft hasn't been ruled out for the contest against the Eagles, but mobility is a big part of his game and cautiousness is the most likely approach for Chicago when it comes to the franchise's biggest star. Bagent, 26, was 5 for 9 for 54 yards after he replaced Williams against the Vikings. He was sacked by Dallas Turner on the final play of the game. Bagent was in line to make his fifth career start. But Johnson got a text message on Tuesday morning that Bagent was going to get evaluated for concussion symptoms, and he had been placed in the concussion protocol. The timeline for his return is unclear. "Honestly, I’m not even in that," Johnson said. "They’ll let me know when he’s available." Chicago, which opened the season with a 59-37 win at the Carolina Panthers, also has rookie Miller Moss on its practice squad. The team has no plans to add another quarterback this week. Johnson said he is looking at the uncertainty as an "opportunity." "I think our guys see it as that as well," he said. "One of those things that everyone outside the building, I am sure, is writing us off and telling us it can’t be done and we really relish that. And so guys will step up to the plate, guys that maybe we don’t anticipate or expect. We have a really talented team." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Roman Reigns Talks WWE Future, The Rock, Cody Rhodes, 'Street Fighter' Role, More
articles.summary: WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns has not been shy about admitting he's at the back end of his career.
articles.body:
WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns has not been shy about admitting he's at the back end of his career.

However, while speaking to Mark Elibert of Complex, Reigns left the door open for another stretch as the face of the company.

"If I stay in shape and I do my end of the job," he said, "I could possibly still have a whole 'nother run that we didn't even think about."

Reigns has done it all in WWE, but he still feels he has unfinished business. The 41-year-old said he feels there are still storylines with "a couple to a few years" of loose ends and "logic gaps" worth revisiting.

"I got like a little bit of OCD when it comes to storytelling and stuff," Reigns said. "I like symmetrical situations, continuity and stuff. ... It's all about the nuances."

Still, Reigns admitted that the next generation is on its way and will take his place at the top when it's time.

"As these young guys continue to grow, they're gonna create matchups and situations for me," Reigns says. "As I'm phasing out and as they're really taking the helm, their superstardom, I think, will create those type of fantasy warfares."

However, Reigns pointed out that there's a lot that goes into being the face of WWE, and only a few Superstars have been able to carry the mantle, namely Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson and John Cena.

"Dwayne is the anomaly. He is the outlier," Reigns said. "Nobody's ever gonna do it like The Rock."

While Reigns and Cena didn't ascend as quickly as Johnson did during the Attitude Era, the OTC now knows what he's looking for in younger Superstars that will determine whether they're worthy of his spot.

"As it's been shown with John and then also with me, it takes a decade or so," he said. "Can you perform every single time and then deliver when you're asked? Can you do it when you're tired? Can you do it when you're sick? Can you do it when you're hungover after WrestleMania? Can you carry the banner for this company? This is a billion-dollar machine. It's not easy."

Reigns named longtime rival Cody Rhodes as the one Superstar who has answered all of those questions.

"There's only been one who's been able to carry that banner," he said. "And that's been Cody."

Reigns has already begun preparing for life beyond pro wrestling, as he's set to star as Akuma in next month's highly anticipated Street Fighter film, which also stars Rhodes as Guile. Reigns said he used elements of his WWE persona to tap into the mind of the popular antihero.

"I think that's why I was considered for the part and got it because there were so many parallels between the Tribal Chief and Akuma," Reigns said. "I said it from the beginning. I'm not a good guy. I'm not a bad guy. I'm the guy, and that's how I've always felt in WWE."

He added about Akuma: "He's not a villain. He just is only looking for the most honorable fight, the greatest competition. That's all he cares about. He's not evil. He just is what he is, and that's what I love about him."

For now, Reigns made it clear that his legacy in WWE is far from over, and he's looking forward to helping to find the next Superstar who can carry the banner for the company.

"It's one thing to have a match with me," Reigns said. "It's another to be the guy that we're working towards to transition from me, or to use my equity to then put a rocket on that guy's back."

He continued, "If you're in the ring with me, your value's going up. It sounds arrogant, but I don't mean it that way. I just mean that if you get in the ring with me, you're gonna get the very best Roman Reigns."

articles.title: El primer Bentley eléctrico en 100 años se llama Torcal, tiene 888 CV y su sonido se ha creado con instrumentos reales
articles.standfirst: El nuevo Bentley Torcal es un SUV de cinco metros capaz de acelerar de 0 a 100 km/h en 2,9 segundos y recuperar 161 kilómetros de autonomía en solo siete minutos.
articles.summary: El nuevo Bentley Torcal es un SUV de cinco metros capaz de acelerar de 0 a 100 km/h en 2,9 segundos y recuperar 161 kilómetros de autonomía en solo siete minutos.
articles.body: Bentley ha tardado 107 años en lanzar su primer coche completamente eléctrico, pero no ha querido estrenarse con discreción. El nuevo Bentley Torcal es un SUV de cinco metros con hasta 888 CV y 1.350 Nm, unas cifras que le permiten acelerar de 0 a 100 km/h en apenas 2,9 segundos. Será también mucho más que un nuevo modelo dentro de la gama. La marca británica lo presenta como el punto de partida de su próximo lenguaje de diseño (que, cuanto menos, es controvertido) y como un anticipo de los futuros Bentley, independientemente de que utilicen motores eléctricos o de combustión. El Torcal emplea dos motores eléctricos y una enorme batería de 113 kWh de capacidad útil, con arquitectura de 800 voltios. Bentley anuncia una autonomía máxima de 600 kilómetros y una potencia de carga de hasta 400 kW, suficiente para pasar del 10 al 80% en menos de 20 minutos o recuperar 161 kilómetros en siete. Números que, como los de prestaciones, están a un altísimo nivel. La gama estará compuesta inicialmente por dos versiones. El Bentley Torcal de acceso ofrecerá 821 CV y 1.194 Nm, hará el 0 a 100 km/h en 3,4 segundos y alcanzará 250 km/h. Por encima quedará el Torcal S, con los mencionados 888 CV y 1.350 Nm cuando se activa el Launch Control, además de una velocidad máxima de 260 km/h. Para que semejantes prestaciones no conviertan el coche en un gigante difícil de manejar, Bentley incorpora por primera vez una suspensión completamente activa. Cada amortiguador puede reaccionar de manera independiente y el sistema prescinde de las barras estabilizadoras convencionales. También equipa dirección trasera de serie, con hasta cinco grados de giro, que reduce el diámetro de giro a solo 11,1 metros. Una de sus soluciones más peculiares aparece al acelerar. Bentley no ha intentado imitar digitalmente el sonido de un V8, sino que ha creado la denominada Dynamic Symphony utilizando grabaciones de instrumentos reales, entre ellos batería, viola y bajo eléctrico. El resultado varía en función de la velocidad y de la presión sobre el acelerador, aunque puede desconectarse para viajar en completo silencio. El interior combina esa experimentación tecnológica con elementos tradicionales de la marca de la B alada. Conserva mandos físicos en la consola y el volante, pero incorpora pantallas OLED curvas, reconocimiento facial y un head-up display con realidad aumentada. Los asientos ofrecen de serie regulación eléctrica en 16 posiciones, calefacción, ventilación y masaje, que opcionalmente puede extenderse también a las piernas. La tecnología llega incluso a las puertas, capaces de abrirse y cerrarse eléctricamente mediante radares. El conductor puede cerrar la suya pisando el freno y los pasajeros, simplemente abrochándose el cinturón. El coche también puede memorizar maniobras de aparcamiento, estacionar desde una aplicación y retroceder automáticamente si encuentra un obstáculo en una carretera estrecha. Pese a ser el Bentley de cuatro puertas más corto de la gama, sus cinco metros permiten ofrecer cinco plazas y un maletero trasero de 460 litros, al que se suma otro compartimento delantero de 90. El Torcal estrenará además el nuevo emblema de Bentley y materiales como el primer tejido para automóviles elaborado íntegramente con lana merina certificada. La marca todavía no ha comunicado su precio.
