articles.title: Court Ruling Opens Door For 2 Indiana Linemen To Play vs. Northwestern
articles.summary: An Indiana state court has opened the door for Hoosiers defensive linemen Stephen Daley and Kellan Wyatt to play against Northwestern.
articles.body: An Indiana state court has opened the door for Indiana Hoosiers defensive linemen Stephen Daley and Kellan Wyatt to return to the playing field for Friday night's Big Ten Conference opener against the Northwestern Wildcats. Monroe Circuit Court Judge Kara Krothe issued a preliminary injunction on Wednesday that grants Daley, Wyatt and more than 90 other athletes a fifth year of eligibility. The NCAA is expected to appeal. For now, though, the ruling clears the way for Daley, Wyatt and dozens of others to return to action. "The 2026-27 Division football, soccer, cross country, and field hockey seasons are underway," Krothe wrote in a 37-page opinion. "Swimming and basketball seasons are fast approaching, with official practices for basketball beginning on September 21. 2026. Spring sports are around the comer. She added: "Plaintiffs have secured roster spots, but will not receive scholarship aid or NIL payments until their eligibility is continued by court order. If relief is denied, they will lose their roster spots. College sports seasons are time-limited opportunities. Once lost, they cannot be restored, even if plaintiffs later prevail on the merits." Daley and Wyatt did not play in Indiana’s 38-0 victory over Western Kentucky last weekend because a temporary restraining order allowing them to compete had expired. Both testified in court last week, but when the decision did not come down before the game, they were held out. Krothe's ruling was expected this week. Daley and Wyatt were starters on last season's national championship team but suffered season-ending injuries before Indiana's playoff run. Neither was selected in April's NFL draft and neither signed an NFL contract to be part of either offseason workouts or training camp. Hoosiers coach Curt Cignetti has repeatedly said he supported the efforts of Daley and Wyatt to get an extra year of eligibility, and he alluded to it again after last weekend's game. "We’ve gotten better since the first game for sure," Cignetti said. "You know, it sure will help if we have Wyatt and Daley. It’s hard to measure that. We’ll find out we think soon. But if not, we lost some key guys last year and other guys stepped up." Wednesday's ruling is the latest twist in a chaotic start to the 2026 college football season, which has been mired in court fights across the country. The NCAA announced in June it was going to adopt a new eligibility model allowing all athletes to compete for five college seasons over five years. The legal fights began when college sports' largest governing body said the new model would not apply to the freshman class of 2022-23. Colorado District Judge Charlotte Sweeney then ruled some members from that freshman class could receive a fifth year of eligibility, a decision that led some players in NFL training camps to consider resuming their college careers. Eventually, Sweeney issued a clarification that pro athletes were not covered by her ruling. That decision was stayed in August by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit, but lower courts, such as the one in Bloomington, have since entered the fray. "Under the plain terms of the 2026-27 NCAA Manual, they are eligible to compete, and the NCAA is breaching its contractual obligations by denying them that opportunity," Krothe wrote. "Harm to the NCAA by virtue of this injunction is minimal or nonexistent. The NCAA regularly grants waivers allowing athletes five years to play, sometimes for hundreds or thousands of athletes at time. This injunction covers less than one hundred athletes across a multitude of sports." Reporting by The Associated Press

articles.title: Inspired By The AL West, Take A Look At The Weakest Playoff Teams In MLB History
articles.summary: With just a few days left in the regular season, the AL West might make a particularly mediocre kind of history.
articles.body: With just a few days left in the regular season, the AL West might make a particularly mediocre kind of history. After Tuesday night's games, the Texas Rangers and Houston Astros were tied for first place at 78-79. No full-season division champion has ever had a losing record. In fact, no team has made the postseason with a sub-.500 record, unless you count a trio of participants from years the playoffs were temporarily expanded: In the 2020 season shortened by the COVID-19 pandemic, Milwaukee and Houston were both 29-31 and made the postseason. In 1981, the Kansas City Royals went 50-53 overall — but they were the AL West's top team in the post-strike second half, meaning they got in. Then in 1994, the Rangers led a woeful AL West at 52-62 when the players' strike ended the season. Every team in the division was under .500 and no postseason was played. MLB expanded its postseason to 12 teams in 2022, raising the likelihood that a sub-.500 team would sneak into October at some point. Just a few weeks ago, it looked like the American League could have several clubs with losing marks in this year's playoffs. The AL Central's Cleveland Guardians and Chicago White Sox have since reached 81 wins, so that won't happen. But the AL West title race could still yield a losing team. In honor of that, here are 10 of the weakest teams to make the postseason, listed in chronological order with their records and run differentials in mind. Note that some of them went on lengthy postseason runs — so don't count out the Rangers or Astros just yet. 1973 New York Mets Record: 82-79 (first in NL East) Run differential: 20 Postseason: Beat Cincinnati 3-2 in NL Championship Series, lost to Oakland 4-3 in World Series The rallying cry was "Ya gotta believe!" from reliever Tug McGraw. It wasn't easy when New York was in last place after an Aug. 30 loss, but the Mets went 21-8 the rest of the way to win the division by 1 1/2 games. Tom Seaver (19-10, 2.08 ERA, 18 complete games) was still at the peak of his powers, and New York held the Reds to eight runs in five games in the NLCS — a series best remembered for a brawl involving Bud Harrelson and Pete Rose. The Mets led the World Series 3-2 and had Seaver starting Game 6, but they couldn't close out the Athletics. 1984 Kansas City Royals Record: 84-78 (first in AL West) Run differential: minus-13 Postseason: Lost to Detroit 3-0 in ALCS The Royals were 11 games under .500 in the middle of July, but they did enough to win the AL West. George Brett hit .284 — his worst average in a 14-year span from 1975-88 — and he was one of just two All-Stars on the team. The other was Dan Quisenberry, who had 44 saves while throwing 129 1/3 innings. He finished second in the Cy Young race behind fellow reliever Willie Hernández of the Tigers. Although Kansas City took the division almost by default in '84, the Royals improved to 91 wins the following year and won the World Series. 1987 Minnesota Twins Record: 85-77 (first in AL West) Run differential: minus-20 Postseason: Beat Detroit 4-1 in ALCS, beat St. Louis 4-3 in World Series Frank Viola was the star of a pitching staff that otherwise offered little — aside from a trio of big names on the downside of their careers. Bert Blyleven allowed 46 home runs, Joe Niekro posted a 6.26 ERA and Steve Carlton made seven largely woeful starts for this Minnesota team. The Twins could hit, though. Kirby Puckett was third in the MVP race, while Kent Hrbek, Gary Gaetti and Tom Brunansky each surpassed 30 homers. Home-field advantage wasn't determined by record back then, so Minnesota had it in the ALCS despite finishing 13 games behind the Tigers, and again in the World Series after being 10 games worse than the Cardinals. The Twins went 6-0 at the Metrodome in the postseason. 1995 Colorado Rockies Record: 77-67 (second in NL West, wild card) Run differential: 2 Postseason: Lost 3-1 to Atlanta in NL Division Series The first wild card in National League history was this Colorado team in a season shortened by the end of the 1994-95 work stoppage. The Rockies' ERA of 4.97 is the worst of the live ball era by a postseason team in a non-DH league. Colorado made up for that, not surprisingly, by leading the NL in runs. Dante Bichette led the league in home runs and RBIs and finished third in batting average. 2005 San Diego Padres Record: 82-80 (first in NL West) Run differential: minus-42 Postseason: Lost 3-0 to St. Louis in NLDS Jake Peavy and a Trevor Hoffman-led bullpen helped San Diego reach the playoffs, but this team never looked the part. The Padres scored the fourth-fewest runs in all of baseball, and their starters went 52-60 with a 4.49 ERA. In the postseason, San Diego never had the lead at any point against the 100-win Cardinals. Game 1 was 8-0 after six innings, Game 2 was 6-1 after seven, and Game 3 was 7-0 after 4 1/2. 2006 St. Louis Cardinals Record: 83-78 (first in NL Central) Run differential: 19 Postseason: Beat San Diego 3-1 in NLDS, beat New York Mets 4-3 in NLCS, beat Detroit 4-1 in World Series The Cardinals won at least 95 games four times under Tony La Russa, but their best postseason success came as a wild card in 2011 and with this team five years earlier. St. Louis nearly blew a seven-game lead in the division in the final two weeks of the regular season, but a roster with Albert Pujols, Scott Rolen, Chris Carpenter and a young reliever named Adam Wainwright always had a chance to get hot. Yadier Molina's homer — and Wainwright's strikeout of Carlos Beltrán — gave the Cardinals the pennant in an epic series with the Mets. 2017 Minnesota Twins Record: 85-77 (second in AL Central, second wild card) Run differential: 27 Postseason: Lost to New York Yankees in wild card game After 103 losses in 2016, the Twins were in first place for a little while before eventually capturing the AL's final postseason spot and losing 8-4 to the Yankees. Byron Buxton played 140 games, the most of his career to date, and Brian Dozier hit 34 home runs. Joe Mauer had moved to first base by this point but was still quite good at the plate, batting .305. Ervin Santana led the rotation in his last good major league season. This team certainly wasn't great, but it was good enough in an AL that produced only five teams above .500. 2023 Miami Marlins Record: 84-78 (third in NL East, second wild card) Run differential: minus-57 Postseason: Lost to Philadelphia 2-0 in NL Wild Card Series The Marlins posted the worst run differential to date by a postseason team — this year's Astros are currently at minus-59 — but Miami went 33-14 in one-run games. The pitching staff with Sandy Alcantara, Eury Perez, Jesus Luzardo and Braxton Garrett helped Miami into the playoffs. Of the Marlins' top 12 players in plate appearances, seven of them finished with negative wins above replacement, according to Baseball Reference. The offense was basically batting champ Luis Arraez, designated hitter Jorge Soler and not much else. Miami lost 93 games the year before this playoff appearance and 100 the year after. 2023 Arizona Diamondbacks Record: 84-78 (second in NL West, third wild card) Run differential: minus-15 Postseason: Beat Milwaukee 2-0 in NLWCS, beat Los Angeles Dodgers 3-0 in NLDS, beat Philadelphia 4-3 in NLCS, lost to Texas 4-1 in World Series Just get in and anything can happen. These Diamondbacks were one of the best examples of that. Arizona started August with nine straight losses to fall below .500, but after doing enough to make the playoffs, they swept two division champions and then won the last two games of the NLCS on the road to capture the second pennant in franchise history. Arizona had a negative run differential in the regular season and was also outscored 30-21 in that series against the Phillies. It didn't matter. 2025 Cincinnati Reds Record: 83-79 (third in NL Central, third wild card) Run differential: 35 Postseason: Lost to Los Angeles Dodgers 2-0 in NLWCS The Reds had a respectable run differential but little star power aside from Elly De La Cruz and the often-injured Hunter Greene. Cincinnati beat out the Mets on a tiebreaker for the NL's final postseason spot — seven games behind the No. 2 wild card — and then made a quick exit. The Reds' best month was 15-11 and their worst was 12-15. Simply avoiding any extended slumps was enough to make the playoffs. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Tello: "No hubiéramos necesitado a Negreira, éramos los mejores"
articles.standfirst: El ex del Barça ha colgado las botas a sus 35 años y da una entrevista en 'Otra Ronda"
articles.summary: El ex del Barça ha colgado las botas a sus 35 años y da una entrevista en 'Otra Ronda"
articles.body: Cristian Tello acaba de cerrar una carrera de 16 años como futbolista profesional. Una trayectoria en la que defendió seis camisetas en distintos países, pero en la que su etapa en el Barcelona ocupa un lugar especialmente importante. El extremo pasó por las categorías inferiores azulgranas, regresó al club después de su paso por el Espanyol y terminó llegando al primer equipo, donde compartió vestuario con algunos de los mejores futbolistas de la historia. En 'Otra Ronda', el programa nocturno de Radio MARCA presentado por Carlos Vicente 'Chitu', Tello echó la vista atrás para recordar aquellos años y explicó cómo vivió su llegada al primer equipo. Guardiola fue uno de los entrenadores que detectó rápidamente sus condiciones. "Me cogió Guardiola y me dijo que no era consciente de las cualidades que tenía", recuerda el exjugador. En los entrenamientos se enfrentaba a defensas como Dani Alves, Adriano o Puyol y, según cuenta, conseguía superarles en determinadas acciones: "Me decía: no eres consciente". Uno de los asuntos que inevitablemente apareció durante la conversación fue el caso Negreira y la sombra que ha acompañado posteriormente a aquella época de dominio azulgrana. Tello admite que le duele que se vincule aquella etapa con el nombre del exvicepresidente del Comité Técnico de Árbitros. "Sí, eso siempre duele", explica. El exfutbolista reivindica el nivel del equipo que vivió desde dentro: "Toda la gente que vio el fútbol es consciente de que no se va a ver un equipo en la vida que juegue al fútbol como jugaba ese equipo". Y añade: "No creo que hiciese falta Negreira ni hiciese falta nadie para ganar los partidos". Tello asegura además que durante su etapa en el vestuario azulgrana nunca tuvo conocimiento de ese asunto. "En la vida había escuchado hablar ni de Negreira, ni en la vida en un vestuario se habla de ningún árbitro", afirma. La historia de Tello con el primer equipo comenzó a construirse cuando Luis Enrique dirigía al Barça B. El extremo explica que entrenar habitualmente con la primera plantilla le permitió demostrar sus condiciones ante los jugadores del primer equipo. Su velocidad y su descaro terminaron llamando la atención de Guardiola. Tello recuerda especialmente su capacidad para jugar sin miedo pese a encontrarse delante con futbolistas de talla mundial. "He sido siempre así, yo creo que eso fue también lo que me llevó a dar el salto de subir al primer equipo", explica. De aquella etapa guarda un recuerdo especialmente bonito. De todos los títulos que conquistó con el Barça, se queda con la Liga de los 100 puntos, lograda con Tito Vilanova en el banquillo. "Fue una Liga muy difícil", recuerda. Y si hay un futbolista que marcó aquella etapa, ese es Leo Messi. Tello reconoce que poder compartir vestuario y entrenamientos con el argentino es uno de los grandes privilegios que se lleva de su carrera. "Me voy a llevar para siempre poder haber jugado y disfrutado de cerca con el mejor jugador del mundo, con el mejor jugador de la historia que va a ser", asegura. Tello destaca especialmente la naturalidad con la que Messi resolvía situaciones que para cualquier otro futbolista parecían extraordinarias: "Disfrutar cada día de un jugador así, lo fácil que lo hacía todo, cómo resolvía partidos, cómo ayudaba a los compañeros". Para el ya exfutbolista, Messi fue y seguirá siendo "un jugador irrepetible".

articles.title: Ex-Auburn coach Bruce Pearl hails Robert Kraft as a hero for banning Macklemore over antisemitic rants
articles.summary: Bruce Pearl calls Robert Kraft a "hero and a patriot" for banning Macklemore from Gillette Stadium, saying silence on antisemitism is complicity.
articles.body: Former Auburn men's basketball coach Bruce Pearl joined "Don't @ Me with Dan Dakich" to defend New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft after Kraft banned rapper Macklemore from Gillette Stadium. Pearl, a prominent Jewish voice in college sports, praised Kraft as a "hero and a patriot" for taking a firm stand against antisemitism. Speaking with Dakich, Pearl argued that Macklemore's messaging crosses from political commentary into overt hate speech. BRUCE PEARL EXPLAINS WHY HE REFUSES TO STAY SILENT ON ISRAEL AND ANTISEMITISM "I think it's great to have this discussion," Pearl said. "Here's where I want to go with what he said, because it wasn't just about hating the Jews. 'Free Palestine,' to Palestinians or to Arabs, means free Palestine of the Jews. How would you free Palestine of the Jews? Well, you either scare them off, run them off, or murder them." During Ed Sheeran's tour at MetLife Stadium, Macklemore sparked controversy with anti-Israel rants and his protest track "Hind's Hall." MACKLEMORE'S LONG HISTORY OF CONTROVERSY FROM GRAMMY WINS TO 'FREE PALESTINE' CONCERT REMARKS Kraft subsequently banned him from Gillette Stadium, citing Macklemore's history of anti-Semitic tropes, including a 2014 Seattle outfit widely condemned as a Hasidic Jewish caricature. Kraft's move triggered a wave of venue rejections, forcing tour promoters to drop Macklemore entirely. Pearl warned that many people repeat activist slogans without understanding their historical weight. "Free of colonization or free of genocide or whatever terms people use, that's not what this means," Pearl stated. "This simply means we're going to do to the Jews in Palestine like we did to them in Egypt, Lebanon, Syria, Iran, or Iraq." BILL MAHER RIPS MACKLEMORE'S GAZA STANCE, SAYS CELEBRITY 'MORAL CONFUSION' IS FUELING ANTISEMITISM Pearl also addressed chants calling to "globalize the Intifada," noting that historical Intifadas involved violent attacks targeting civilians on buses, in hotels, and in the streets. "Asking for somebody's death is not free speech," Pearl emphasized. "It is hate speech, and it should not be allowed." Pearl emphasized that leaders cannot remain silent when witnessing hate. MIKE HUCKABEE CALLS OUT MACKLEMORE ON ANTISEMITISM: 'VOICE' OF 'JEW HATRED' "We grew up in a time where Dr. King talked about silence as complicity," Pearl told Dakich. "Therefore, as a coach, when we see something wrong... we take action because our silence as teachers and educators is complicity." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Pearl concluded that Kraft showed rare leadership in protecting his community: "Robert Kraft is the owner of a business. He has a responsibility as a leader in the community. When given the opportunity, he did not remain silent and he went and did something. You know what? Sometimes actions have consequences, but sometimes inaction is actually worse. Robert Kraft is not a coward. He is a hero, and he is a patriot." articles.title: Bills news: D.J. Moore's injury update puts Week 3 return in play
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills will be facing the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 3, and they may be getting one of their key receivers on the field. After suffering an AC j...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills will be facing the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 3, and they may be getting one of their key receivers on the field. After suffering an AC joint sprain against the Detroit Lions , D.J. Moore was back at practice for the Bills, and it sounds like everything is good with him health-wise.

"Felt great. Still gotta go through some things, but we're going to be good," Moore said via Matt Parrino of Syracusedotcom.

Shortly after Moore was injured in the game , it seemed as if he dodged any sort of major injury, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network at the time.

"It means that it's probably the best-case scenario. I mean, landed hard. You know, all the Twitter doctors were kind of up in arms about, you know, reading his eulogy and all that," Rapoport said. "And then it's like sprain AC joint day-to-day. We'll see if he's able to play next week.

"They got kind of a little extra time, obviously, because they played on Thursday, but not major, separated shoulder essentially, which is what an AC joint sprain is. I think he should be okay long term for sure. So definitely good outcome for the Bills."

It would be good for the Bills to have Moore suit up, as they've been on a tear to start the season. Josh Allen looks like he's better than last season, which would be crazy, but he's doing everything an MVP would do. Even if Moore isn't able to play, they should be fine for the time being.

In the end, the most important thing is that Moore is 100% and that he can make an impact at a high level for the Bills when he's on the field.

articles.title: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. doesn’t regret comments about Blue Jays contract after down season
articles.summary: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. knows he has nothing to apologize for.
articles.body:
After coming just two outs short of a World Series title last season , the Toronto Blue Jays were hoping to capitalize on that momentum this year. That momentum never quite materialized as the Blue Jays were officially eliminated from the playoffs on Wednesday and will likely finish under .500 for the season, too.

One of the biggest reasons the Blue Jays struggled in 2026 was a slump season from the face of the franchise, Vladimir Guerrero Jr .. At the time of this writing, the six-time All-Star has just nine home runs, his lowest RBI total since 2020, and has slugged below .400 for the first time in his career. He will also finish with the worst OPS (.695) of his career by far. In related news, for a guy known for hitting massive dingers, he didn't mash a home run at home in Toronto until September 13th .

At face value, you could understand why Blue Jays fans have been distraught about the 27-year-old Guerrero's subpar performance during what is supposed to be the middle of his prime. And, again, at face value , you could understand why some fans might be upset about recent comments Guerrero made on a podcast where it seemed like he inelegantly noted that he got his 14-year, $500 million contract because of what he had accomplished before, not what he will do in the future.

Amid some festering outrage, Guerrero Jr. addressed these comments through his Spanish-language interpreter. Predictably, he regrets nothing because the snippet of the podcast everyone saw was not what he meant:

It's a harsh truth for fans when one of their favorite players performs poorly, but high-level athletes like Guerrero are, in fact, paid handsome contracts for what they did before and what they will do in the future. This isn't a "he only cares about money" situation. It's acknowledging the reality that anyone who thinks Guerrero doesn't deserve his deal after an awful 2026 is wrong, because he still does.

Plus, as Guerrero notes, he signed his half-billion deal before last year . You know, the same year he took the Blue Jays to the brink of a championship. It sucks that he followed up that season with arguably the worst year of his career, but he still earned the money as one of baseball's most prominent stars. And knowing his well-established reputation, whenever the next MLB season takes place, Guerrero should be back to playing like a titan soon enough.

articles.title: Chargers work out 4 players before making decision at long snapper
articles.summary: The Chargers ultimately signed long snapper Spencer Triplett after working out four players ahead of Week 3.
articles.body:
The Chargers worked out four players, including long snapper Spencer Triplett , before ultimately signing him to the practice squad.

The signing of Triplett comes after the Chargers elevated Marquez Valdes-Scantling from the practice squad to the active roster. The move followed the decision to place tight end David Njoku on injured reserve.

Njoku will miss at least the next four weeks. He will be eligible to return when the Chargers take on the Rams in Week 8.

Triplett now replaces Valdes-Scantling on the practice squad.

The rookie long snapper joins the Chargers after a six-year career at North Carolina . In 2023, Triplett was part of a Tar Heels operation that converted 22 of 24 field-goal attempts and all 51 extra-point attempts.

Triplett entered the 2025 season on the Patrick Mannelly Award Watch List, which recognizes the best long snapper in college football each year.

articles.title: Vikings veteran Aaron Jones has a knee injury to work through after his 23-carry, 105-yard game
articles.summary: The productivity Aaron Jones gave the Minnesota Vikings last week came with a price, in the form of a knee injury that has clouded the 10th-year veteran runn...
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. (AP) — The productivity Aaron Jones gave the Minnesota Vikings last week came with a price, in the form of a knee injury that has clouded the 10th-year veteran running back's status for the upcoming game.

Jones was held out of practice Wednesday for treatment on the injury that occurred during his 23-carry, 105-yard performance in steady rain at Chicago . The Vikings play Sunday at Tampa Bay.

"He's one of one as far as toughness," coach Kevin O'Connell said. "He's a really good football player and is just as good as it gets from the leadership and establishing the standard of what we want Minnesota Vikings football players to look like. I know he's going to do everything in his power to try to make it this week, and hopefully we'll have him out there on Sunday."

Jordan Mason , who led the Vikings in rushing last season, was placed on injured reserve last week because of a broken thumb. He must miss at least three more games. After Jones, the only other non-fullbacks on the active roster are Deejay Dallas and rookie Demond Claiborne, a sixth-round draft pick from Wake Forest. Behind them are recent practice squad additions Jerome Ford and Jarret Patterson.

Dallas, Ford and Patterson have a combined 14 years of NFL experience, but none of them were in training camp. Dallas was signed to the practice squad just before the season opener.

Even if Jones is cleared to play, the Vikings will undoubtedly be cautious with his workload against a Buccaneers defense that has allowed an average of just 3 yards per rush — fourth-best in the league — after ranking fifth in the NFL in rushing yards against last season.

The return of quarterback Kyler Murray from a concussion also raises the question about how much he'll be willing to scramble, having missed most of his debut and the game last week because of a hit to the head at the end of a run.

"This is going to be a challenge to try to run the football," O'Connell said, "and we've got to try to meet it."

For Jones, there's rarely a physical challenge he's not ready for. His 23 attempts last week matched the third-most of his career, the most since he carried the ball 24 times for Green Bay on Nov. 13, 2022, at Dallas. He topped the 100-yard mark for the first time since Nov. 24, 2024, at Chicago .

Jones even had his helmet popped up by a hit so hard it cut his cheek.

"He knew that it was a grinding game. The surface was not ideal, but we knew that we had to run the ball effectively and Aaron knew that his role was to run it," left guard Donovan Jackson said. "When he came back to the huddle he was just like, 'Hey, man, just give me some space, and I'll make it work.'"

Jones took a pay cut to come back this season, and the Vikings likely wouldn't have had the same amount of confidence they do in elevating their running game if he had not returned.

"You just can't put into words how much he means to our team. It's not just leadership and it's not just being maybe the most amazing human being on the planet," O'Connell said. "It's a football thing, too."

articles.title: Presidents Cup 2026: Thursday's fourball matchups, starting times, analysis
articles.summary: The first session features five fourball matches, the first of which tees off at 12:35 p.m. ET.
articles.body:
The 16th Presidents Cup gets underway on Thursday at Medinah Country Club's No. 3 Course outside of Chicago.

The first session features five fourball matches, the first of which tees off at 12:35 p.m. ET. The par-4 first hole for the competition is usually the fifth hole for members, with the 18th hole of the alternate routing being the regular fourth hole.

Thursday's session will be followed by a five-match foursomes session on Friday, two four-match sessions of each team format on Saturday, and a 12-match singles session on Sunday.

articles.title: Wyndham Clark hopes to shed villain label at 2026 Presidents Cup
articles.summary: The format of the Presidents Cup offers Wyndham Clark a chance at redemption no other American golfer in Chicago this week can conjure.
articles.body:
MEDINAH, Ill., — Wyndham Clark was preparing for his practice round shot in the arena-style first tee box at the 2026 Presidents Cup , and paused briefly when he heard a variation of his new catchphrase.

"Let's open some grape this weekend, Wyndham," a fan shouted from above.

A grin quickly appeared and then disappeared from Clark's face as he stood over the ball. This was a variation on the remark he made famous this season after winning the U.S. Open in June while being heckled by fans at Shinnecock Hills unhappy he was atop the leaderboard. "We're definitely opening up some grape. A lot of grape," Clark said at the time in regards to how he would celebrate.

Golfers who have won PGA Tour events in 2026 season

"All my buddies call it grape – vino or grape – and that one came out," he explained on Wednesday when he met with reporters before being paired with Collin Morikawa for the first set of four-ball matches on Day 1 of the Presidents Cup . "Now, any time I see somebody, they're like, 'Let's open up some grape.' This week, during practice rounds, I've probably heard it 15 times. 'Let's open up some grape.'"

The format of the Presidents Cup offers Clark a chance at atonement no other American golfer here in Chicago this week can conjure. The USA vs. International format has naturally led to a warmer reception for Clark and the Denver native hopes the environment can help aid the process of altering how he's viewed.

"Since New York, it's been all love," Clark insisted.

But there's more than love, Clark acknowledged, in changing perceptions.

"I think if it didn't happen throughout my career, that would be a bummer," Clark said. "Even though maybe the media has made me out to be kind of the villain, if you will, I don't feel like I'm that person, and eventually it would be nice if people were rooting for me and someone else was the underdog. We'll see. Hopefully things are trending and changing the right way."

Clark's strong play this year has only complicated the matter.

He has three wins in 2026, including the second major of his career. But his past missteps are still fresh for golf fans.

Clark damaged two lockers in the men's locker room at the 2025 U.S. Open at Oakmont when he missed the 36-hole cut. Pictures of the damage went viral on social media following Clark's exit from the tournament. The club subsequently banned Clark and he had to complete anger management counseling and donate to charity to smooth the situation over.

A month before that, at the PGA Championship at Quail Hollow, he threw his driver after a bad tee shot on the 16th. The club hit a sponsor sign and knocked it over a few feet from the man holding the flag.

Playing some of the best golf of his career hasn't quieted the concerns and reputational damage done by his past outbursts. He's the rare golfer who's on a roll and also seeking redemption.

So this week at the Presidents Cup, wearing red, white and blue may do more for his image than a whole bottle of grape.

"I really want to have a couple of those moments that are just iconic and really bring the crowd together and get the team going," Clark said.

articles.title: Walker Jenkins' pinch-hit RBI single in the 7th keys Twins' 4-2 victory over Giants
articles.summary: Pinch-hitter Walker Jenkins hit an RBI single in the seventh inning that put Minnesota ahead and the Twins won their second straight over the San Francisco G...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Pinch-hitter Walker Jenkins hit an RBI single in the seventh inning that put Minnesota ahead and the Twins won their second straight over the San Francisco Giants with a 4-2 victory on Wednesday.

The score was 2-all with Kody Clemens at second and one out in the seventh. Jenkins delivered a base hit to right off Dylan Smith (0-6) that scored Clemens for a 3-2 Minnesota lead. With two outs, Josh Bell added an RBI single off Sam Hentges to increase the Twins' edge to 4-2.

Yoendrys Gomez (3-4) retired all five hitters he faced to earn the win. Andrew Morris worked a scoreless ninth for his fifth save. He struck out Shay Whitcomb with runners at first and second to end the game.

Minnesota got on the board first when Luke Keaschall took Cesar Perdomo deep to left for a solo homer in the third inning. It was Keaschall's 10th homer of the season.

The Giants scored both of their runs with two outs in the fourth on Whitcomb's pop-fly single that fell just fair near the right-field line. It gave San Francisco a 2-1 advantage.

The Twins tied it in the fifth on Keaschall's sacrifice fly that scored Ben Ross, who had tripled.

Perdomo, a rookie left-hander, gave up two runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings. He struck out two and did not issue a walk.

Minnesota starter Connor Prielipp, also a rookie left-hander, allowed two runs on four hits in 5 1/3 innings. He struck out three and walked two.

With the loss, the Giants fell to 37-41 at home, meaning they will have a losing record for the season at Oracle Park.

Twins RHP Joe Ryan (6-10, 3.83 ERA) faces the visiting Rangers on Friday night.

Giants RHP Yunior Marte (0-1, 4.66) takes on the visiting Dodgers on Friday night.

articles.title: Tigers news: Justin Verlander makes 100 pitch declaration before final start
articles.summary: Justin Verlander would probably pitch forever if his body allowed him. Instead, one of the greatest pitchers of his generation will take the mound for the fi...
articles.body:
Justin Verlander would probably pitch forever if his body allowed him.

Instead, one of the greatest pitchers of his generation will take the mound for the final time Saturday when the Detroit Tigers host the Pittsburgh Pirates at Comerica Park. Verlander apparently has no interest in making his farewell a ceremonial appearance.

A.J. Pierzynski revealed on Foul Territory that Verlander plans to pitch "until my arm falls off" in his final start. The 43-year-old also gave Pierzynski an ambitious goal for his final afternoon on a major-league mound.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"If I can make it to one hundred pitches, I'm going to do it," Verlander said, according to Pierzynski.

Whether manager A.J. Hinch and the Tigers actually allow that is another question. Verlander has made only one MLB start this season after hip and hamstring injuries derailed what was supposed to be his final campaign. He hasn't gone through anything resembling a normal starter's buildup, making 100 pitches extremely ambitious.

But what exactly is Verlander saving his arm for now?

Detroit has been eliminated from postseason contention after entering 2026 with much different expectations. The Tigers eventually became sellers, trading Tarik Skubal to the Dodgers and moving other pieces as their season unraveled. Now the final weekend is largely about celebrating a franchise legend.

The perfect ending would be Verlander somehow pitching deep into Saturday's game before Hinch eventually makes that walk toward the mound. Imagine 8 2/3 innings, Comerica Park on its feet, and Verlander handing over the baseball one final time.

Three Cy Young Awards, an MVP, two World Series championships, three no-hitters, and more than 3,500 strikeouts have already secured Verlander's place among baseball's greats. He just wishes that another championship would have happened in Detroit.

Saturday isn't about adding anything else to that résumé.

It's about emptying the tank one last time.

articles.title: Jackson Koivun goes from NCAA title to Presidents Cup debut in 112 days
articles.summary: Only four years ago, Jackson Koivun played in the Junior Presidents Cup as a high school senior and wandered around Quail Hollow Club a little star struck be...
articles.body:
MEDINAH, Ill. (AP) — Only four years ago, Jackson Koivun played in the Junior Presidents Cup as a high school senior and wandered around Quail Hollow Club a little star struck being around the likes of Scottie Scheffler and Xander Schauffele and Justin Thomas.

It was only 112 days ago when Koivun helped lead Auburn to another NCAA title , the final chapter in a remarkable college career.

And on Thursday, the 21-year-old Koivun plays with Thomas in a fourballs match for his Presidents Cup debut. For a sport with a reputation of moving slowly, his career has been at warp speed.

"Definitely going to feel some nerves on the first tee, but we're all human. I think everyone does," Koivun said Wednesday. "I told Justin once I get my first tee shot out of the way, I'm going to be good. Just kind of balancing adrenaline, nerves, everything like that to the best of my ability."

Three days of practice on the No. 3 course at Medinah Country Club — rain-soaked when they arrived, drying out by the day — gives way to the opening session of five fourballs matches.

The Presidents Cup has a heavy favorite in the Americans — they have won the last 10 times and lost only once since the matches against the Internationals began in 1994 — and a sentimental favorite in Adam Scott , who has is playing for the 12th time without ever being on the winning side.

"History is history, and it's nice to be a part of history on the good side," Collin Morikawa said. "But history can always be changed. I think for us, starting tomorrow, it all starts 0-0."

U.S. captain Brandt Snedeker wasted little time sending out world No. 1 Scheffler and Sam Burns against Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im.

They will be followed by Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele against the Japanese duo of Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune; Thomas and Koivun against Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria; Morikawa and Wyndham Clark against Scott and Ryan Fox; and the anchor match of Chris Gotterup and Patrick Cantlay against Si Woo Kim and Tom Kim.

"You kind of have an idea of how this thing's going to go and got a good game plan set forth," Snedeker said. "And now it's just about getting out of these guys' way and let them go do what they love to do."

"I think everyone comes into these tournaments with optimism," International captain Geoff Ogilvy said. "They're very momentum-based tournaments."

Ogilvy thought back to two years ago at Royal Montreal when the Americans made a big opening statement with a 5-0 shutout. The Internationals responded with a shutout of their own in foursomes in which three of the matches didn't even get to the 15th hole.

"You could never have predicted that," Ogilvy said, a vice captain in 2024. "We've been thinking about this for a long time. So we're just excited to get going."

The United States has another embarrassment of riches compared with the Internationals. With only five matches on opening day, Snedeker sat Russell Henley, the No. 6 player in the world, and Jacob Bridgeman, who came into his first Presidents Cup fresh off another PGA Tour victory.

It also has Koivun, one of the more intriguing characters in these matches considering how quickly he made it to this stage. Koivun won in his third start as a professional in the 3M Open — Scheffler was the runner-up — and Snedeker trusted his gut in picking him.

He wasted no time giving Koivun a taste of the matches.

"Jackson being a young kid, I feel like he's really kind of found his way on our team really quickly," Snedeker said. "I feel like he's handled the adjustment really well. Justin is just a natural pairing for him. I think he'll do a great job putting his arm around him and show him how USA golf is meant to be played."

Koivun already has had a memorable week. As the only player who came without a plus-one, the Americans had him pose with the Presidents Cup trophy with all their wives and girlfriends. Clark told of the grief Koivun caught when he was the last one to show up for the bus ride to Medinah.

They all have high hopes for him between the ropes.

"The fact that he has the maturity and the correct outlook on everything, he's obviously really competitive and he's obviously really talented," Thomas said. "I'm excited for him this week. It's going to be an awesome experience for him."

The Americans have won the opening session eight of the last nine times.

"We would love to be in front, have a winning session," Ogilvy said. "That's the job tomorrow is to win a session. I'm sure we'll be in good moods either way, but the goal would be to win the session."

articles.title: Should you start any Browns WR in fantasy football in Week 3?

articles.body:
The Browns ' offense is not loaded with the most promising fantasy assets. The unit is young and still developing, but the quarterback play holds most of it back to an extent.

During the 2026 season here on Browns Wire, we will review all fantasy-relevant skill players for the team and share whether they are worth a start.

Each position has players that can help or hurt your fantasy team, so this will be a form of start or sit. In this piece, we will be looking at the Browns wide receivers. After weeks of suggesting starting either KC Concepcion or Jerry Jeudy, we are going to pivot.

Denzel Boston is leading rookie wide receivers in most categories, so the connection is there with Deshaun Watson. Thus, we are saying to sit Jeudy and Concepcion and start Denzel Boston.

The latter is worth a spot in your lineup at the flex spot, but understand he is slightly touchdown-dependent.
